title: Exposure-adjusted anomaly routing for intraday telemetry
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: our current intraday anomaly alerts for usage / cost / latency produce a high rate of false positives during rapid product exposure changes (beta rollouts, marketing-driven traffic, feature flags). These false positives increase on-call fatigue and reduce trust in the alerting pipeline. Goal: build a routing and enrichment layer that adjusts baseline calculations and alert thresholds in near real-time based on exposure signals (feature flag cohorts, rollout waves, campaign tags), suppresses expected variation, and forwards only actionable anomalies to the core alerting service with provenance metadata so Console teams can surface cause and remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Exposure metadata (feature flag / rollout / campaign) is joined to intraday telemetry stream for >= 95% of events within 60s of ingestion.
Anomaly forwarder tags anomalies with exposure provenance and a confidence score; Console Alerts UI displays exposure reason and recommended action.
False positive rate on historical beta rollouts drops by >= 45% in evaluation window (retrospective run against last 6 months of rollout events).
No observable increase in median pipeline end-to-end latency beyond 200ms for non-enriched telemetry (goal: <1% regressions).
Runbook entries and on-call playbook created and linked in ticket; alert severity mapped to existing paging rules.
Automated suppression rule exists for scheduled large-scale marketing campaigns (configurable TTL and whitelists).
tasks: Instrument exposure tags in ingestion layer (Kafka topic change + Avro schema update)
Implement streaming enrichment job (Beam/Flink) that joins telemetry with exposure store and computes exposure-adjusted baseline
Add routing logic in anomaly-forwarder service to apply suppression / threshold scaling based on exposure signals
Persist per-customer short-term baselines (Redis) with TTL; periodic snapshot to ClickHouse for backfill and audits
Add provenance fields to alert payload (exposure_reason, exposure_id, adjusted_threshold, confidence)
Integration tests + retrospective evaluation against 6 months of telemetry and 12 known rollouts
Dashboard: expose 'suppressed anomalies' metric and a rollout-correlated view in Console
Create runbook and add escalation mapping for exposure-related anomalies
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Console PM + SRE. Agreed success criteria and non-goals (we will not change core anomaly models, only routing/enrichment).

2026-02-18: Prototype enrichment join implemented in dev cluster (Beam). Joining via consistent customer_id + rollout_tag works for 94% of test events. Observed 30ms median added latency for enriched path.

2026-02-24: Design review with infra: compared Redis vs Bigtable for per-customer short-term baseline storage. Chosen: Redis cluster with eviction TTL 48h for hot paths, snapshots to ClickHouse for auditing. Rationale: sub-100ms lookup SLA and simple eviction semantics.

2026-02-28: Safety decision: suppression will be opt-in per team. PMs can flag a rollout as 'suppressible' with a TTL; default is no suppression. Added requirement to surface suppression status in Console.

2026-03-03: First integration test run on 3 months of telemetry + 7 rollout events. Preliminary results: 52% reduction in alerts during rollout windows, 6% reduction overall (signal preserved outside rollouts). Planning retrospective evaluation on full 6 months next week.

2026-03-05: Began work on alert payload schema update (GH PR opened). Noted compatibility concern with older alert consumers; added feature-flagged rollout for forwarder to emit new fields only when negotiated with consumer.
notes: Technical approach: streaming join of telemetry -> exposure store (materialized from LaunchDarkly + internal rollout registry) -> compute exposure-aware baseline using EWMA with per-cohort weights. We will not train an ML model in this phase to keep explainability for on-call teams.

Performance considerations: enrichment must be idempotent and resilient to partial exposure store outages. Plan: fall back to non-enriched routing (emit 'exposure_unavailable' tag) rather than blocking alerts.

Operational trade-offs: Redis TTL introduces potential cold-start false positives after TTL expiry. Mitigation: warm-up heuristics for customers with frequent traffic and conservative thresholds for cold baselines.
Security/Privacy: exposure metadata can contain campaign identifiers; treat as PII-level-1 and ensure masking in public dashboards. Audit will be requested for the ClickHouse snapshots.
Compatibility: alert consumers that don't understand provenance fields will see unchanged primary fields; we will use feature negotiation header to enable new fields per-consumer.
Rollout plan: start with internal teams + one pilot customer (beta) for two weeks, then open to broader customers. Metrics to watch: suppressed_alerts_ratio, alert_precision, median_triage_time.
